h1: The 7 Best Budget NAS for Beginners of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Budget NAS for Beginners: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven beginner-friendly network storage boxes compared on software, bays, RAID and networking, from ready-to-run to 2.5GbE.
summary: The UGREEN DH2300 is the best overall starting point for its easy software and 2-bay flexibility. Synology DS223 is the pick if you value guided setup above price. The Buffalo LinkStation 210 is the simplest ready-to-run option, and the TerraMaster F2-425 gives you room to grow.
intro: Many first-time NAS buyers fall into the same trap: they buy the cheapest enclosure, then discover the real cost is the hard drives and the hours spent learning the software. A NAS is a small always-on computer, and how friendly its interface is matters more for a beginner than raw speed.

We reviewed seven network storage options and ranked them on the spec sheets and product listings: software approach, bay count, RAID support, networking speed and whether drives are included. We left out a USB-attached RAID enclosure because it connects to one computer and is not network storage.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DH2300 2-Bay Desktop NAS (Diskless)
products.verdict: The easiest on-ramp to a proper 2-bay NAS at a modest price.
products.description:
The DH2300 is a diskless 2-bay desktop NAS running UGREEN's UGOS software, which is pitched at newcomers. It supports RAID 0 and 1, handles up to 64TB total, and uses Gigabit Ethernet.

It ranks above the Synology because it sits in the $100-200 bucket rather than $200-500 and still gives you mirrored storage. You give up the deep ecosystem of Synology's software, but for backups and shared folders the gap is small for a beginner.

Buy it if you want a clean first NAS and are happy to supply your own drives. Remember that Gigabit networking caps transfer speed, so it will not feel instant with large video files.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers who want simple software and mirrored drives.
products.skipIf: You need faster than Gigabit transfers.

products.name: Synology DS223 Home & Office Backup Hub (2-Bay Diskless NAS)
products.verdict: The most guided setup here, at a higher price.
products.description:
The DS223 is a 2-bay diskless NAS built around Synology DSM, a mature operating system with centralized file access, monitoring and RAID 1 mirroring. Networking is Gigabit.

It sits just behind the UGREEN because it costs more, in the $200-500 bucket, for hardware that is similarly modest. What you pay for is software polish and a long track record of update support.

Choose it if your biggest worry is getting stuck during setup and you will use the NAS for years. If budget is tight, the UGREEN gets you most of the same result for less.
products.idealFor: Beginners who want the smoothest software and will keep it long term.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest entry price.

products.name: Buffalo LinkStation 210 2TB 1-Bay NAS (Drives Included)
products.verdict: Plug in, share files, done: no drive shopping required.
products.description:
A 1-bay NAS that ships with a 2TB drive already inside and is preconfigured out of the box. It offers home cloud and network storage over Gigabit Ethernet, with no RAID because there is only one drive.

It ranks third since the single bay means no redundancy: if the drive fails, your files go with it. Against the UGREEN and Synology, you trade protection and flexibility for a much simpler start and no extra purchases.

It suits people who just want shared storage and a backup target today. Keep a second copy of anything important, because there is no mirroring here.
products.idealFor: True beginners who want storage running without buying drives.
products.skipIf: You want mirrored drives or room to expand.

products.name: Asustor Drivestor 2 Gen 2 AS1202T 2-Bay NAS (Diskless)
products.verdict: 2.5GbE networking in the lowest price bucket.
products.description:
A 2-bay diskless NAS with a quad-core 1.7GHz CPU, 1GB DDR4 RAM and 2.5GbE networking. It also supports 4K media serving.

It ranks fourth because 1GB of RAM is thin for anything beyond file sharing, while the TerraMaster below carries 4GB. Its edge over the UGREEN is the faster 2.5GbE port at a similar price.

Pick it if you have a 2.5GbE router or switch and want quicker transfers. If your network is Gigabit, that advantage goes unused.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers with a 2.5GbE network who stream media.
products.skipIf: You plan to run many apps at once.

products.name: TerraMaster F2-425 2-Bay NAS (Intel x86 Quad-Core, Diskless)
products.verdict: More CPU and RAM than a beginner needs today, useful tomorrow.
products.description:
A diskless 2-bay unit with an Intel x86 quad-core CPU, 4GB RAM and 2.5GbE LAN, with multimedia server support. It lands in the $200-500 bucket.

It ranks below the Asustor on value because you pay noticeably more, but it has four times the RAM and the more capable x86 processor. That headroom matters if you add apps or media transcoding later.

Buy it if you expect your NAS needs to grow. If you only want backups, the extra cost is hard to justify.
products.idealFor: Beginners who expect to run more apps over time.
products.skipIf: You only need simple file backup.

products.name: Buffalo LinkStation 210 6TB 1-Bay NAS (Drives Included)
products.verdict: Same simple box as the 2TB, with three times the space.
products.description:
This is the same preconfigured 1-bay LinkStation as the 2TB version, shipping with a 6TB drive and Gigabit Ethernet. There is still no RAID.

It ranks below the 2TB because it moves into the $200-500 bucket while keeping the single-drive risk. More space in one drive means more to lose at once if it fails.

Choose it if you have a lot of files to store and want zero setup. Pair it with an external backup, since one failure would take everything.
products.idealFor: Beginners with lots of photos or video and no wish to configure RAID.

products.name: Beelink Mini PC ME Pro 2-Bay NAS (Intel N95, Diskless)
products.verdict: A mini PC that doubles as a NAS, not a simple appliance.
products.description:
The ME Pro pairs an Intel N95 CPU with 12GB LPDDR5 RAM and a 128GB M.2 SSD, plus two hard drive bays and three M.2 SSD slots. It has dual LAN and works as a mini PC, file server and NAS.

It ranks last for beginners because it is more flexible than friendly: you manage an operating system rather than a guided NAS app. In exchange, it has the most RAM and expansion of anything here.

Buy it if you enjoy tinkering and want one box for several jobs. Pure beginners should start with the UGREEN or Synology.
products.idealFor: Tech-curious buyers who want a mini PC and NAS in one.
products.skipIf: You want a simple guided appliance.

methodology.title: Software friendliness
methodology.description: We favored guided, beginner-oriented interfaces over general-purpose operating systems that demand more setup knowledge.

methodology.title: Data protection
methodology.description: Bay count and RAID options were weighed, since a single drive offers no protection from failure.

methodology.title: Network speed
methodology.description: Gigabit versus 2.5GbE ports were compared, as the network link caps real file transfer rates.

methodology.title: Hardware headroom
methodology.description: CPU and RAM on the spec sheet were judged against realistic beginner and growth workloads.

methodology.title: Total startup cost
methodology.description: Whether drives are included changes the true price, so we counted that in the value ranking.

whatMatters.detail: NAS software is the interface where you create folders, users and backups. A beginner-oriented system saves hours of confusion and reduces the risk of misconfigured sharing. Look for names such as UGOS or DSM and read whether setup is described as guided.

A bay holds one drive, and RAID 1 mirrors two drives so one can fail without data loss. Without it, a single drive failure erases everything stored. Check the listing for the words RAID 1 and the number of bays before buying.

Diskless units cost less up front but need you to buy compatible NAS drives. Drive-included units are ready immediately but limited in size. Look for the word diskless in the title and add drive cost to your budget.

Gigabit Ethernet tops out around 110 megabytes per second in practice, while 2.5GbE is roughly two and a half times faster. It only helps if your router or switch also supports 2.5GbE. Check both the NAS port speed and your own network gear.

These set how many apps and media streams the NAS can handle at once. Plain file storage needs little, but 4K media serving benefits from more. Check the CPU model and RAM figure in the bullet points instead of assuming.

cards.label: Diskless
cards.text: You choose and buy the drives, which gives you control over capacity and lets you use RAID 1 across two bays. The UGREEN DH2300, Synology DS223, Asustor AS1202T and TerraMaster F2-425 all work this way.

cards.label: Drives included
cards.text: The unit arrives ready to use with a drive inside, cutting setup decisions, but you get one bay and no RAID. The two Buffalo LinkStation 210 models fit here.

howToChoose.note: Most beginners with files they care about should default to a diskless 2-bay unit and mirror two drives.

howToChoose.subheading: For Photo and Family Backup Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Two bays with RAID 1 so a drive failure does not lose irreplaceable photos, plus simple software that automates backups from phones and PCs.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The UGREEN DH2300 offers RAID 1 with beginner software at a lower price, and the Synology DS223 does the same with more polish.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want long-term software support and polish, which points to the Synology DS223, or CPU headroom for media apps, which the TerraMaster F2-425 offers.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mainly need shared folders and one backup copy. The UGREEN DH2300 or the Buffalo LinkStation 210 2TB handle that for less.

faq.q: Do I need to buy hard drives separately?
faq.a: For diskless models like the UGREEN, Synology, Asustor, TerraMaster and Beelink, yes. The Buffalo LinkStation 210 models include a drive. Budget for NAS-rated drives, since they are built for continuous running.

faq.q: What is the biggest beginner mistake?
faq.a: Treating a NAS as a backup by itself. RAID protects against one drive failing, not against deletion, ransomware or theft, so keep a second copy of important files elsewhere.
Only if your router or switch also supports it. Otherwise you pay for speed you cannot use, and the UGREEN at Gigabit is a better value.
Guided systems like Synology DSM and UGREEN UGOS walk you through creating a volume and user accounts. The Buffalo LinkStation is preconfigured and is the least work.

faq.q: How do I maintain a NAS?
faq.a: Keep the firmware updated, watch drive health alerts and make sure the unit has airflow. Replace a failed drive in a mirrored setup promptly.

faq.q: Why did you leave out the QNAP TR-004?
faq.a: It connects by USB to one computer, so it is direct-attached storage rather than network-accessible. It does not fit a guide about NAS devices.

finalTake: The UGREEN DH2300 is our top choice for most beginners, with friendly software, RAID 1 and a modest price. Pay extra for the Synology DS223 if guided setup is your priority, or take the Buffalo LinkStation 210 for a no-fuss box with a drive included. Pick the TerraMaster only if you plan to grow into heavier use.
